text:
maria: quick sanity check — i'm landing a terraform change to let our staging SA (IRSA role) use the data KMS key. added an aws_kms_grant resource but i'm fuzzy on the right principal and whether to include an encryption context constraint. anyone seen pitfalls?

jun: use the IAM role ARN (the role created for the serviceaccount) as grantee_principal, and set operations to Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey. prefer explicit encryption_context_subset if you can (limits blast radius). e.g.
```hcl
resource "aws_kms_grant" "staging_sa" {
  name              = "staging-myservice-grant"
  key_id            = aws_kms_key.data.key_id
  grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.eks_irsa_staging_myservice.arn
  operations        = ["Encrypt", "Decrypt", "GenerateDataKey"]
  constraints {
    encryption_context_subset = {
      "redwood:env" = "staging"
      "redwood:sa"  = "my-service"
    }
  }
}
```

jun: important: grantee_principal must be the role ARN (not the serviceaccount string). IRSA -> role mapping gives you that role.

ashley: also double-check the key policy. if the key policy is too restrictive, the grant creation will fail (or the role can't use the key). add a statement allowing CreateGrant for the IAM principal that manages the grant (usually the deploy role), and allow UseKey for the grantee. quick snippet to check: `aws kms get-key-policy --key-id <key-id> --policy-name default`

ashley: if you want safe rollout, create the grant via the infra CI role (the deployer) so Kubernetes pods can't create grants themselves. we had a subtle race where pods assumed grants existed before apply.

maria: note — i'm creating the iam role via tf too (module.eks_irsa.role). the role's assume_policy is the usual OIDC WebIdentity with condition on `sts:aud`= `sts.amazonaws.com` and `sub` = `system:serviceaccount:staging:my-service`. should be fine.

jun: yeah good. also annotate the SA in k8s: `kubectl annotate sa my-service -n staging eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn=arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/eks-irsa-staging-my-service` :eyes:

ops-bot: terraform plan: +1 to aws_kms_grant.staging_sa, +1 to aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.eks_irsa_policy (no other diffs). plan id: plan-20240301-9a3

maria: ran apply in staging branch in ci, waiting for pod test.

deploy-bot: applied to staging, verified that pod can decrypt: `kubectl exec -n staging my-service-6df4c -- curl -s http://localhost:8080/health --header "X-Encrypted-Key: true"` returned 200 and logs show successful kms.Decrypt call.

ashley: nice — did you see any CloudTrail denies? (common when policy missing)

deploy-bot: cloudtrail: no AccessDenied for kms:Decrypt in the last 10m for role/eks-irsa-staging-my-service.

maria: awesome, thanks everyone. I'll follow up with a small PR to add the encryption_context tags to the key policy docs so next time it's less fuzzy. resolved :white_check_mark:
